diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists constants $\Upsilon,\Lambda^*$ such that for any $\Upsilon\geq \Upsilon'$ and $\Lambda\geq \Lambda^*$

issues.failure_explanation: The paper says the method is more general than T-coercivity theory and handles broader, high-contrast coefficients. The analysis itself rests on T-coercivity and needs Upsilon = sigma^+_min/sigma^-_max sufficiently large (Lemma well, lm1, and the theorems require Upsilon >= Upsilon'). The theory therefore covers only the regime where the positive coefficient dominates the negative one. The experiments use (sigma^+,sigma^-) = (1,3), (1,10^3) and (1,10), i.e. Upsilon = 1/3, 10^-3 and 0.1, which is not the large-Upsilon regime (the random-inclusion case is the opposite regime). The generality claim and the robustness claim are not supported by any result, and the tested regimes are not covered by the analysis.

failure_location.quote: In comparison, the proposed method presented in this paper is more general, as it can handle a broader range of coefficient profiles, including those with high contrast ratios.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to the large-Upsilon regime covered by the theory. State explicitly that the experiments with Upsilon <= 1 are beyond the proven regime, or add analysis for small Upsilon.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised scope (more general than T-coercivity, robust for high-contrast sign-changing media) is unsupported by the theorems. The numerical evidence lies outside the hypotheses of the error analysis.
issues.title: Claim of greater generality and high-contrast coverage contradicts the large-Upsilon theory and the tested regimes
issues.why_classification: Repair is a rewording of the scope claim, but it removes an advertised advantage and exposes a theory/experiment gap, so more than a local fix.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The detailed proof can be found in \cite{ye2024}.

issues.failure_explanation: Inequality (coer s) is stated with an undefined operator P_H. It is later used (lem1, lem2, prop:exponential decay) as a lower bound in terms of ||pi z||_{s}, which has to be a different quantity. The constant C_2 combines the term Lambda^{-1}||R||_1/sqrt(Upsilon), while (coer s) has Lambda^{-1}||R||_0/sqrt(Upsilon). The definition (eq:norm1 of R) bounds ||grad R w||_{Omega^-} by ||grad w||_{Omega^-} for w in V(Omega^+), where grad w on Omega^- is undefined. No proof is given in the paper. Coercivity of s(pi v, pi T v) requires pi to commute with restriction to Omega^+ and Omega^-, which is never stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define P_H (presumably pi), correct (eq:norm1 of R) and C_2, state the needed alignment of pi with the interface, and give a proof of (coer s) and C_2 in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: The coercivity constant C_2, used in every decay estimate and in the inf-sup argument, is not established as written.
issues.title: Lemma well: undefined operator P_H, inconsistent constants, proof delegated
issues.why_classification: A contained re-derivation fixes it, but the pi-versus-interface compatibility needs a genuine argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $\norm{\mathcal{R}_H'}_1$ should be understood as a positive constant such that for all $v\in \Omega^+$.

issues.failure_explanation: v_1 and v_2 are v restricted (zero-extended) to Omega^+ and Omega^-. Knowing pi v = 0 gives pi(v 1_{Omega^+}) = 0 only if every coarse element lies in Omega^+ or Omega^-. This is never assumed, and the random-inclusion test does not satisfy it. Without it, T_H v = v_1 - Q_H pi T v in Omega^+, the traces on Gamma are not those of v_1, and the form {v_1, -v_2+2R_H' v_1} is not valid. The estimate I_1 >= (1 - ||R_H'||_1/sqrt(Upsilon))||v||^2 then fails. The constant ||R_H'||_1 is also left as an unspecified constant.

failure_location.quote: Here, the terms $\mathcal{Q}_H \pi v_1$ and $\mathcal{Q}_H \pi v_2$ vanish because $\pi v=0$ on each coarse element

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an explicit hypothesis that the coarse mesh resolves Omega^+/Omega^-, or redo the T_H analysis for non-aligned interfaces. Quantify R_H' and show the I_1 estimate.
issues.overall_effect: T-coercivity of B on tilde V, hence the global inf-sup constant and the global/multiscale error estimates, is not established for general interfaces.
issues.title: lm1: vanishing of Q_H pi v_1 and Q_H pi v_2 is unjustified (needs interface-aligned coarse mesh)
issues.why_classification: Adding an alignment assumption is a short fix but excludes the non-aligned examples used. The general case needs a contained new argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the last second inequality comes from the boundedness of the $\mathcal{T}_H$ under the $s$-norm

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma well gives the constants C_0, C_1 only for T. In lm1 (term I_2) and glothm, the same constant C_1 is used for T_H = T - Q_H pi T. Lemma interpolation controls Q_H only through C_inv, which is not controlled in terms of Upsilon, Lambda or H, and it bounds the a-norm rather than the s-norm. Only 'bounded' is claimed, with no constant. T-coercivity also requires T_H to be bijective, which is never shown.

failure_location.quote: Recalling the boundness of $\mathcal{Q}_H$, we can see that $\mathcal{T}_H$ is a bounded operator that maps from $\tilde{V}$ to $\tilde{V}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove bijectivity of T_H on tilde V. Derive explicit a- and s-norm bounds for T_H including C_inv, and track them in epsilon_0 and the later constants.
issues.overall_effect: The T-coercivity constant epsilon_0 and the constants in the global error bound are not controlled.
issues.title: lm1: bounds for T (eq:bound s, eq:bound a) applied to the modified operator T_H; bijectivity not shown
issues.why_classification: A contained new lemma on T_H restores the argument without changing the architecture, though constants change.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then, we reduce the proof of the inf-sup stability  of $\mathcal{B}(v, \mathcal{T}_Hv)$ for all $v \in \tilde{V}$.

issues.failure_explanation: The paper claims inf-sup stability of B on V_glo with a constant beta_glo. What is shown (lm1) is T-coercivity on tilde V = {pi v = 0}, and V_glo is the B-orthogonal complement of tilde V by lm3.2. Stability on tilde V does not by itself give a lower bound for the inf-sup quantity over V_glo, since no stable projection or Fortin operator onto V_glo is constructed. The constant beta_glo is not related to epsilon_0 or ||T_H||. It is then used in cea and thm:main local.

failure_location.quote: suggests that it suffices to check that

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove that the inf-sup constant on V_glo follows from the T-coercivity on tilde V and the orthogonal splitting V = V_glo + tilde V, with an explicit beta_glo.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised inf-sup stability of the global and multiscale spaces rests on an unproved reduction.
issues.title: Global inf-sup on V_glo asserted via a 'Fortin trick' without argument
issues.why_classification: It needs a new lemma but fits the existing framework.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof gives ||u-u_glo||_a^2 <= (1/epsilon_0) (f, T_H(u-u_glo)) <= (C_1/epsilon_0) ||f||_{s^{-1}} Lambda^{-1/2} ||u-u_glo||_a. The factor 1/epsilon_0 is dropped in the displayed chain, and the constant C_1/epsilon_0 is absent from the statement. The statement claims constant 1, and the norm is written s^{-1} instead of tilde s^{-1}.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the estimate with the constant C_1/epsilon_0 and use tilde s^{-1}.
issues.overall_effect: The global estimate holds only with an uncontrolled constant C_1/epsilon_0 that depends on Upsilon.
issues.title: glothm: stated constant omits C_1 and 1/epsilon_0 produced by the proof
issues.why_classification: Local correction of the constant; the rate and method survive.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: providing that $\frac{1}{\Lambda}$ and $C_*$ are small enough ($\frac{1}{\Lambda}, C_*\leq 1)$

issues.failure_explanation: The I_4 bound gives C_* ||z||_a^2 + C_* Lambda ||pi z||_s^2, so the proof needs C_2 - C_* Lambda > 0 to get the constant C. The stated conditions are 1/Lambda <= 1 and C_* < 1, which do not imply C_* Lambda < C_2 (Lambda >= Lambda^* is large and C_2 < 1). The claim 'p_1 >= p_2 >= 0' is therefore unsupported. The true requirement is C_1 mu_msh^{-1} k^2 H^2 <= C_* Lambda < C_2, i.e. kH bounded independently of Lambda, which is stricter than the stated resolution condition (eq:res). The decay rate theta depends on C and so inherits the problem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the resolution condition by C_1 mu_msh^{-1} k^2 H^2 <= C_* min{Lambda, 1} with C_* small. Recheck C, theta and the thresholds Lambda^*, Upsilon'.
issues.overall_effect: Exponential decay, and all results using it, are proved only under a stronger resolution condition than the one stated, or with C <= 0 (no decay).
issues.title: lem1: positivity of C_2 - C_* Lambda not implied by the assumed parameter conditions
issues.why_classification: A limited strengthening of the hypothesis repairs it; the result stays comparable but the regime shrinks.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: there exists constants $\Upsilon,\Lambda^*$ such that for any $\Upsilon\geq \Upsilon'$ and $\Lambda\geq \Lambda^*$

issues.failure_explanation: Summing the i-wise k^2 terms, each estimated by the global quantity ||z||, produces a factor N (the number of coarse elements, about H^{-2}). The lower bound C'' therefore requires C_* N < C_2. This is inconsistent with the resolution condition (eq:res) (C_* < 1 independent of N) and with the claim of H-independent constants. The coercivity lower bound should use min, not max. The positivity claimed ('>0') is not established. The threshold Upsilon' is never defined.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Sum the k^2 terms before estimating, so that k^2(z, T z) is bounded once by C_*(||z||_a^2 + Lambda ||pi z||_s^2) with no factor N. Use min in C'' and define Upsilon'.
issues.overall_effect: The global decay estimate and the constant c_0(Lambda) hold as stated only if C_* is O(1/N), a far stronger resolution requirement (about k H^{1+d/2} small).
issues.title: prop:exponential decay: constant C'' involves N and a max; its positivity is unjustified
issues.why_classification: The estimate can be restructured within the existing argument, though constants and the statement need rework.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the multiscale solution $u_{\mathup{ms}}$ of \cref{cemvar} exists and is unique.

issues.failure_explanation: prop:exponential decay bounds ||(G^m - G^inf) phi|| by c_0 C_ol (m+1)^d theta^{m-1} ||pi phi||^2, but the proof of the inf-sup bound drops this factor. It sets eta = C_*' H^{-1}, whose constant does not contain theta^{(m-1)/2}. Such an eta is large as H -> 0 and not small. Smallness, needed for 1/2||v_ms|| <= ||v_glo|| <= 3/2||v_ms|| and for beta_cem > 0, only holds when (m+1)^{d/2} theta^{(m-1)/2} H^{-1} is small, i.e. m >~ |log H|. Hence the inf-sup stability and unique solvability are not proved for every m >= 1. The m=1 entries of the tables (energy error 24.57, 1.11, 1.01) show the method breaking down.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the factor (m+1)^{d/2} theta^{(m-1)/2} in eta. Assume m >= m_0(H, Lambda, Upsilon) so that eta is small, and restate the existence, uniqueness and Cea results with that hypothesis.
issues.overall_effect: The claims of inf-sup stability of V_ms, and of existence and uniqueness of u_ms for every m >= 1, are unsupported. Stability holds only for sufficiently many layers.
issues.title: cea: perturbation parameter eta = C_*' H^{-1} cannot be small; the decay factor was dropped
issues.why_classification: The structure survives with an added oversampling hypothesis; an existence statement for all m is weakened.

issues.failure_explanation: (i) The proof multiplies by alpha/beta_cem, where alpha contains H^{-1}. The statement says C_cem depends only on Upsilon^{-1} and beta_cem, so the bound ||u-u_ms|| <= C_cem(...)||f|| hides a factor H^{-1}. With ||f||_{s^{-1}} = O(H) and the first term Lambda^{-1/2} ||f||, this gives O(1), not O(H). (ii) For m = 4|log H|/|log theta|, H^{-2} theta^{(m-1)/2} (m+1)^{d/2} is of order (m+1)^{d/2} ~ |log H|^{d/2}, so the bound is O(H |log H|^{d/2}) even ignoring (i). (iii) The d in (m+1)^{d/2} is not tied to the stated dimension R^2. (iv) The conclusion C_cem^{-1}(k)||f|| is malformed.

failure_location.quote: In particular, if $m\geq 4|\mathup{log} (H)|/|\mathup{log} (\theta)|$, then we have optiaml order convergence in $H$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use an H-independent continuity constant in cea (a direct Poincare bound of the k^2 term). Choose m >= C|log H| with a larger constant to absorb (m+1)^{d/2}, or state the rate with a log factor.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised optimal first-order rate in H is not proved. The proof yields a quasi-optimality constant growing like H^{-1} and a logarithmic loss.
issues.title: thm:main local: optimal O(H) claim and constant independence not supported (H^{-1} in alpha, log factor)

diagnostic_evidence.quote: and for the constant $C_1$, we use the resolution condition \cref{eq:res} again to obtain the estimate that $C_1$ depends on $k^{-1}$.

issues.failure_explanation: C_1 is defined in Lemma well through Upsilon and ||R||_0 only and does not depend on k. The resolution condition (eq:res) is an upper bound on k^2 H^2, so it cannot produce a k^{-1} dependence. The proof gives C_1 Lambda^{-1/2}||f||, with no k^{-1}. The stated bound has a factor that grows as k -> 0, which is not derived. For k > 1 it claims a gain that is not proved.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove k^{-1} from the statement, or derive and state the actual k-dependence of the constants.
issues.overall_effect: The k-dependence in the stated estimate is unsupported.
issues.title: thm:main local: spurious k^{-1} factor in the error bound
issues.why_classification: Correcting the stated dependence is local and leaves the method, rate and scope unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: our multiscale method demonstrates greater flexibility and accuracy when suitable oversampling layers are selected, compared to the conventional $Q1$ FEM

issues.failure_explanation: In the flat-interface table, Q1 FEM at H=1/80 has relative energy error 2.152e-05, while the m=4 multiscale error is 1.713e-04, about eight times larger. The m=4 error also increases from H=1/40 (5.66e-05) to H=1/80. The L2 error shows the same pattern (1.203e-05 versus 5.386e-06 is not better in the way claimed for energy). The claim and the conclusion's repeat hold only for H=1/20 and 1/40, not for the finest coarse mesh.

failure_location.quote: We can see that for $m=4$, the proposed multiscale method exhibits higher accuracy than the $Q_1$ FEM.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the claim to H=1/20 and 1/40, and discuss the loss of accuracy at H=1/80 for fixed m.
issues.overall_effect: The reported accuracy advantage over Q1 FEM is overstated and the observed non-convergence at m=4 is not acknowledged.
issues.title: Numerical claim of higher accuracy than Q1 FEM contradicted by the table at H=1/80
issues.why_classification: Only the wording of an empirical comparison must be corrected; no theorem is affected.
